# Architecture for SQLite Backup Guide

Project: `peerfoil-fixture-doc` · Assurance: Guided · Revision: 1 · Status: accepted

- **Author:** architect (claude-code, anthropic-claude, session null)
- **Written at:** 2026-10-20T08:40:00Z
- **Decisions applied:** d-0001, d-0002, d-0003, d-0004
- **Quality Contract:** `.peerfoil/quality.md` revision 1
- **Reviews:** rv-0001

## Goals

Produce one short Markdown how-to guide, `guide.md`, that teaches a solo developer to
back up a small SQLite database safely. The finished first phase covers making a backup
with the sqlite3 .backup command, verifying that the backup opens, and restoring from it.
Every factual claim names its source and every link resolves.

## Users

The reader is a solo developer who keeps one SQLite database file on their own computer
and uses a terminal. The reader must not be exposed to advice that risks their data, such
as copying a live database file, and must not need any tool beyond sqlite3 and a shell.

## Boundaries

Inside the project: the single file `guide.md` and its examples. Outside: automation
scripts, scheduled backups, server or multi-user setups, and any other document. The
guide relies on the existing sqlite3 command-line tool instead of describing a custom
backup program.

## Dependencies

| Dependency | Purpose | License | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | The guide is plain Markdown; its examples name the reader's own sqlite3 tool | — | sqlite3 is referenced, not shipped |

## Data

None. The guide handles no data of its own. Its examples use a synthetic database file
name, `notes.db`, and dated backup names; no real data, keys, or identifiers appear.

## Risks

| Risk | Response |
|---|---|
| A reader copies a live database file and gets a corrupt backup | The guide warns against plain copies and teaches the .backup command first |
| An example command drifts from current sqlite3 behavior | The link and source checks run before each phase closes |
| Unsourced claims go stale unnoticed | Requirement r-0002 makes every factual claim name its source |

## Accessibility

The only surface is a Markdown document. It uses real headings in order, descriptive
link text, numbered lists for sequences, and fenced code blocks for anything typed, so it
meets the structural WCAG 2.2 Level AA criteria that apply to static text. The pack's
readability review and render check confirm this before publication.

## Security

The guide is static text with no inputs or execution. Its example commands must be safe
to copy as written: they only read the database and write a new backup file, never delete
or overwrite the original. No command in the guide may call the network.

## Privacy

No personal data. The examples use synthetic file names only, and the PeerFoil records
for this project contain no names, addresses, or identifiers.

## Licensing

The guide is the user's own work and carries no third-party text. Quotations, if any are
added later, must name their source and keep within the source's license terms.

## Open decisions

d-0004 is assumed (plain second-person prose for a solo developer). No decision is open.
